label: Intelligibility of a thing: Intel: Respect is the respect of being knowable, that is, of standing…
term: intelligibility of a thing (being knowable by intellect)
definition: intel : Respect is the respect of being knowable, that is, of standing in relation to an intellect as its object or as conformed to it (ST I q.16 a.1, a.3). Has x intel says x is intelligible; MoreIn intel x y says x is more intelligible than y. It is a respect like truth and being; nothing identifies it with either, and its links to them are the open premises STMT-TRUTH-OF-THINGS-IS-INTELLIGIBILITY and STMT-INTELLIGIBILITY-PROPORTIONED-TO-BEING. It is not a human observer's actual knowing (q.16 a.1 calls that relation accidental) nor sentence truth (DISAMB-TRUE).
note: Stipulative respect motivated by claims AQUINAS-ST-I-Q16-A1-TRUTH-OF-THINGS-A and AQUINAS-ST-I-Q16-A3-BEING-AND-INTELLIGIBILITY-A; the passages relate truth, knowability and being but do not define a comparative of intelligibility, which remains an analyst reading.
